Subject: Draft: 14-day pilot sprint canvas + mutual action plan (MAP) — initial GDoc

Hi Elena / team,

As discussed on the call this morning, attached is a lightweight MAP template we usually use for short pilots. I converted it into a 14-day sprint canvas so we can get to a meaningful acceptance decision quickly.

Summary (what's in the GDoc):
- Day-by-day milestones (setup, integration, data validation, evaluation, sign-off)
- Clear owner for each milestone (Redwood vs. Solvatech)
- Acceptance criteria: latency/throughput targets, quality checks, security checklist pass
- Risk & mitigation table (most immediate: sample size for eval, access to test dataset)

Ask of you: please take a look at the canvas and tell us the following by EOD Tuesday:
1) Any missing stakeholders (security/infra/legal) we should include on the MAP
2) Acceptance criteria that would be considered sufficient for Solvatech to move from pilot -> PO (i.e., sign-off)
3) Preferred time windows for a 30-minute alignment session this week to finalize the first cut

Links & attachments:
- GDoc (editable): https://docs.google.com/document/d/1A2b3SolvatechMAP
- Attached: pilot-scope-brief.pdf (2pp overview)

Attachments: solvatech_14day_map_gdoc_link.txt, pilot-scope-brief.pdf

Thanks — I kept this intentionally short so we can iterate in the doc.

Best,
Soojin Lee

Subject: Re: Draft: 14-day pilot sprint canvas + mutual action plan (MAP) — initial GDoc

Thanks Soojin — appreciate the fast turnaround and the clear canvas. Quick notes after a first pass:

- Procurement: we'll need a short T&C appendix in the MAP for procurement to track (purchase order timeline, billing contacts). I've cc'd procurement.
- Security: Diego (cc'd) will review the security checklist; he flagged that we need the SOC2 report and an overview of data retention for test logs.
- Acceptance criteria: from Solvatech's side we'd like to see: 1) average 95th percentile latency < 220ms for our 1k-token queries, 2) semantic accuracy measured on our 250-case eval set with >= 87% correctness for top-3 responses, and 3) no failures with PII leakage in the sample runs.

For the alignment session, available windows: Wednesday 10/20 10:30–11:00 PT or Thursday 10/21 14:00–14:30 PT. Friday is tight for us.

I'll add Diego's initial comments to the GDoc and loop back.

—Elena

Elena — thanks for the early acceptance criteria; those are helpful and concrete. I've made two suggested edits in the GDoc (comments inline):

1) Added a performance-metrics row to the MAP: expected metric, measurement method (synthetic traffic vs. replay), and owner. Suggest Redwood measure latency on replay and Solvatech confirm on synthetic.
2) Tightened the 'Sign-off' language to require a joint post-mortem doc for any failed acceptance criteria and a rollback plan for production rollout.

I'm pasting the key changes here for visibility:
- For latency: measure 95th percentile on our replay harness; target <220ms. Owner: Redwood infra (Marissa).
- For quality: evaluation script and gold labels live in the GDrive folder; we'll run a batch eval on day 12 and share the notebook. Owner: Solvatech / Elena to confirm dataset access.

If the team prefers, I can convert the MAP into a slide (one-slide visual) for your execs before the call. That usually helps procurement and security reviewers.

—Marissa
